rows.definition: DeviceMemoryProfile.CachePlanningAvailable in internal/compute/device_memory_profile.go requires established positive cache capacity, allocation alignment, and subgroup width before ROCm QSA or Vulkan scratch policy can make a cache-bounded planning decision (#12440).
rows.distinction: This predicate checks whether the device facts needed for planning are available. DeviceCacheTileTokens then computes a tile size from those facts. Neither operation establishes physical cache residency or performs a device allocation.

rows.definition: DeviceMemoryProfile.CacheCapacityBytes in internal/compute/device_memory_profile.go records the selected device's established cache capacity in bytes. Consumers must also check CacheCapacityKnown; a numeric zero or an unknown device is not a default Halo capacity (#12440).
rows.distinction: This is the device capacity input to scratch policy, not the bytes currently allocated or a measured cache occupancy. DeviceCacheTileTokens uses this budget to calculate a bounded K/V tile; CachePlanningAvailable requires it alongside alignment and subgroup facts.

rows.definition: DeviceCacheTileTokens in internal/compute/device_memory_profile.go computes the largest subgroup-aligned token count whose separately aligned K and V buffers fit the explicit device cache budget. Missing facts, invalid sizes, and arithmetic overflow produce an unavailable result (#12440).
rows.distinction: This is a software sizing calculation using an established DeviceMemoryProfile, not the KV cache that stores tensors. CachePlanningAvailable checks prerequisite facts without calculating a tile. The computed fit is not a measurement of physical cache residency.
